- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or shift downward.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.67) but model forecasts flat or declining, model underestimates upside; increase forecast by 1–3% relative to recent mean or sentiment-weighted trend.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 60+ day high), model often holds or overcorrects; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average or sentiment-weighted median.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and model forecast is trending sharply, reduce forecast slope to avoid overreaction; use sentiment as smoothing factor for trend adjustment.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 5–7 days, model is lagging; adjust early forecast to match sentiment-driven volatility or recent price momentum.
